To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a) a differential SC amplifier with programmable output offset and gain has been designed and successfully integrated into a 0.25 um CMOS process, and b) a new differential CMFB circuit with reduced errors and faster settling time has been proposed.
a differential SC amplifier with programmable output offset voltage and gain, intended to interface a fully differential pressure sensor with an ADC has been designed, implemented, and characterized.
the circuit has been successfully designed, implemented and tested in a SoC device.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and characterization of a low power differential SC amplifier for processing a differential input signal coming from pressure sensors.
the design of a differential SC amplifier for processing a differential pressure sensor input signal.
the design and analysis of a low-power, fully differential switched-capacitance amplifier for processing a differential input signal coming from an interface of pressure sensors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the circuit has been successfully implemented in a SoC device and that the design has been proven to work properly.
the design of a low power differential SC amplifier for processing fully-differential input signals coming from pressure sensor interface is successfully completed.
a differential SC amplifier with programmable offset has been successfully designed and implemented.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a fully integrated pressure sensing system, which includes an SC differential amplifier, a SC CMFB, an ADC and a microcontroller, is able to achieve an overall power consumption of 1.3 mW and an effective resolution of 10.5 bit.
the design of the differential SC amplifier is a good example of the use of SC technique in low-power and low-voltage applications.
we have developed a differential SC amplifier with programmable output gain and offset voltage, suitable for interfacing low-level pressure sensors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed SC amplifier can be used to implement a programmable gain and offset voltage amplifier in a SoC device with very limited silicon area and low power consumption.
the proposed differential SC amplifier is able to achieve high linearity, high CMRR and high PSRR while keeping low power consumption and small silicon area.

it shows how the use of a differential OTA error cancellation technique, combined with the use of a symmetrically loaded SC CMFB, can lead to the design of low-power SC circuits with very good linearity.
